FEG Hackathon 2026 
EU & Croatia Regulatory Compliance Guide for Participants 
Track: Croatian brand (PSK) | As of 4 September 2026 
Purpose & Scope 
This guide translates the compliance considerations flagged for FEG Hackathon 2026 into practical build 
guidance for teams working on the Croatian brand (PSK) track. It is an awareness summary for a 
hackathon proof-of-concept, not legal advice, and does not replace a compliance/legal review — which is 
required before any solution moves beyond the hackathon. 
Official Ground Rules (as communicated to participants) 
Common ground rules for all challenges: solutions must comply with the EU regulatory baseline 
(GDPR, ePrivacy, AMLD/KYC, eIDAS 2.0, EU AI Act, accessibility per EAA/WCAG 2.1 AA) and with 
responsible gambling principles — no dark patterns, no inducements targeting vulnerable or self-
excluded customers, 18+ verification respected throughout. Anonymized, synthetic or sample data 
only. 
 
What Each Requirement Means for Your Build

Area What it covers What this means for your build Reference 
eIDAS 2.0 Electronic 
identification, e-
signatures/seals, trust 
services, and the EU 
Digital Identity Wallet 
(EUDI Wallet). 
If age or identity verification is part of your concept, 
referencing the EUDI Wallet pattern (attribute-based 
proof, e.g. “over 18” without sharing full ID) is a good 
forward-looking design choice. 
Reg. 910/2014 
eIDAS 2.0 
(2024/1183) 
EU AI Act Risk-based rules for AI 
systems (prohibited / 
high-risk / limited-risk 
/ minimal-risk). 
Manipulative or 
exploitative AI 
practices are 
prohibited outright. 
Any AI/ML feature (recommendations, risk scoring, 
personalization, fraud/AML detection) must avoid 
manipulative dark patterns and must not exploit 
vulnerabilities — this is the same principle behind the 
“no dark patterns” ground rule. 
A “Digital Omnibus on AI” entered into force 27 July 
2026, deferring high-risk-system obligations by up 
to 16 months — check the current in-force 
provisions/timeline. 
Reg. (EU) 
2024/1689 
Accessibility 
(EAA / WCAG 
2.1 AA) 
Accessibility 
requirements for 
consumer-facing 
digital services — 
perceivability, 
operability, 
understandability, 
robustness. 
Build demo UIs with basic accessibility in mind: 
sufficient colour contrast, keyboard navigation, alt 
text on images, readable font sizes. 
Directive 
2019/882 
WCAG 2.1 AA 
 
Responsible Gambling & Player Protection 
• No dark patterns: no manipulative UX designed to nudge continued play, spending, or re-engagement 
(e.g. disguised ads, forced continuity, fake urgency). 
• No inducements to vulnerable or self-excluded customers: no bonus offers, free bets, or 
push/marketing content targeted at accounts flagged as at-risk or self-excluded. 
• 18+ verification respected throughout: age-gating should apply at every relevant entry point in your 
prototype, not only at registration. 
• EU soft-law baseline: Commission Recommendation 2014/478/EU sets non-binding principles (risk 
information, deposit/spend limits, self-exclusion, staff training, responsible advertising). Croatia's 
national rules (see below) make several of these binding. 
 
Data Rule — Anonymized, Synthetic or Sample Data Only 
No real player or customer data, no real identity documents, and no live production data feeds or APIs may 
be used in any hackathon build. Use only anonymized, synthetic, or provided sample datasets — this 
applies across every requirement above and is non-negotiable regardless of a challenge's technical scope. 
Croatia (PSK) National Layer 
EU regulations set the floor; Croatian national law adds binding requirements on top, particularly for 
gambling/player-protection controls. Source: FEG compliance research (Sept 2026). 
--- Page 3 ---
Fortuna Entertainment Group 
FEG Innovation Hackathon 2026 —EU & Croatia Compliance Guide | Page 3 of 4 
Area National layer — Croatia (PSK) 
Data protection Act on the Implementation of the GDPR (Zakon o provedbi Opće uredbe o zaštiti 
podataka) — supervised by the Croatian Data Protection Agency (AZOP). 
Gambling / responsible 
gambling 
Act on Games of Chance (Zakon o igrama na sreću) plus its implementing Regulation 
on Measures for Socially Responsible Organisation of Games of Chance — this is 
binding, not soft law: it requires ID/age verification and a check against a register of 
excluded players before play is allowed. Regulator: Ministry of Finance. 
Build any “self-exclusion” or “age-gate” concept in your prototype as a register-check 
pattern, not just a UI checkbox. 
AML / KYC National AML framework (Zakon o sprječavanju pranja novca i financiranja terorizma) 
— administered by the Anti-Money Laundering Office under the Ministry of Finance. 
Digital Services Act Croatia has adopted an implementing act for Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (DSA), 
designating national authorities and penalties — relevant if your solution has platform, 
marketplace, or user-generated-content features. 
Gaps to note Croatian-level transpositions/authority designations for ePrivacy, eIDAS and the AI Act 
were not independently confirmed in the source material used for this guide — the EU-
level instrument in the table above still applies as the floor. 
 
Other EU Instruments Flagged by Compliance (Background 
Awareness) 
These were also shared by the compliance team. Most are not directly triggered by a short hackathon POC 
but are useful context if a challenge touches these areas, or for anything progressing beyond the 
hackathon. 
Instrument What it covers / status Relevance to a hackathon build 
NIS2 Directive Directive (EU) 2022/2555 
Cybersecurity risk-management and incident-
reporting duties for essential/important entities (18 
sectors, size thresholds apply). 
Hackathon POCs are almost certainly 
below scope thresholds. Good 
practice only: basic security hygiene 
(no hard-coded secrets, no real 
credentials, secure-by-design). 
EU Data Act Reg. (EU) 2023/2854 
Access/portability rules for data generated by 
connected (IoT) products and data-processing 
services; fair (FRAND) data-sharing terms. 
Relevant only if your solution involves 
connected devices or cloud data 
portability/switching features. 
Digital Services Act 
(general) 
Reg. (EU) 2022/2065 
Transparency and content-moderation obligations 
for online intermediaries/platforms; stricter tier for 
very large platforms. 
Relevant if your build has user-
generated content, ads, or a 
recommender system; see also the 
Croatia-specific DSA note above. 
EDPB Guidelines 
4/2019 (Art. 25 
DPbDD) 
EDPB guidance 
Practical guidance on the “data protection by 
design and by default” obligation already required 
under GDPR Art. 25. 
Use as the practical how-to for the 
GDPR privacy-by-design point above. 
Digital Omnibus 
package 
Commission proposal page 
Two strands: the AI strand entered into force 27 Jul 
2026 (defers AI Act high-risk timeline). The 
data/GDPR/ePrivacy/NIS2 strand is still under 
negotiation, not expected before late 2026. 
Rules affecting the AI Act and, later, 
GDPR/ePrivacy may keep shifting — 
re-check before any post-hackathon 
build-out. 
--- Page 4 ---
Fortuna Entertainment Group 
FEG Innovation Hackathon 2026 —EU & Croatia Compliance Guide | Page 4 of 4 
Instrument What it covers / status Relevance to a hackathon build 
CSRD Directive (EU) 2022/2464 
Corporate sustainability reporting duties for large 
companies (narrowed in 2026 to >1,000 employees / 
>€450m turnover). 
Corporate-level reporting obligation, 
not a technical build requirement — 
background only unless your 
challenge specifically involves ESG 
data/reporting features. 
CS3D (CSDDD) Summary 
Supply-chain human-rights/environmental due 
diligence for very large companies; scope narrowed 
and transposition delayed to 26 Jul 2028 
(compliance from 2029). 
Corporate-level, long transposition 
runway — background only. 
EU Taxonomy Reg. (EU) 2020/852 
Classification system for “environmentally 
sustainable” economic activities, used alongside 
CSRD reporting. 
Background only, unless a challenge 
track is specifically about 
sustainability/ESG data. 
 
Sources 
Core ground-rule instruments and the Croatia national-layer summary are drawn from FEG compliance-team 
research (Legora EU & Croatia regulatory compliance guides, Sept 2026) and the EUR-Lex texts linked throughout. The 
“Other EU Instruments” section reflects publicly available guidance current as of September 2026 and may change as 
the Digital/Data Omnibus negotiations conclude. 
Disclaimer 
This guide is an awareness summary prepared for FEG Hackathon 2026 participants. It is not legal advice and does 
not replace a compliance or legal review. Any solution progressing beyond the hackathon into a real build must be 
reviewed by FEG Legal & Compliance before it processes any real data or goes live.
